Lunch meat pinwheels only require a few very specific ingredients, like some honey roasted turkey breasts and some ham. Make lunch meat pinwheels with help from a private chef in Boston in this free video clip.

Expert: Matthew Harker
Contact: www.matthewharkerevents.com
Bio: Matthew Harker's passion for the art of cooking began as a child, spending time in the kitchen with his Calabrese and Galician grandparents.
Filmmaker: Ryan Shelby

Series Description: It doesn't take a professional chef to learn new kitchen skills or whip up a tasty snack the whole family can enjoy. Learn how to make quick snacks with help from a private chef in Boston in this free video clip.

summary.brief: Chef spreads honey‑mustard on a lavash wrap, layers turkey, honey‑roasted ham, Swiss cheese, tomato and lettuce, rolls it tightly, secures it with toothpicks, slices it into pinwheels and plates the bites.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a series of eHow branding graphics and music. Chef Matthew Harker, wearing a bright blue chef coat with rolled‑up sleeves, appears at a granite countertop. White plates hold the ingredients: a lavash wrap, honey‑mustard dressing, roasted turkey slices, honey‑roasted ham, Swiss cheese, sliced tomato and lettuce. Using a brush he spreads an even layer of honey‑mustard over the flat wrap, then adds thin, even layers of turkey, ham, cheese, tomato and lettuce across the surface. He rolls the wrap tightly from one end into a cylindrical log, inserts a toothpick about every inch to keep the roll together, and slices the log with a sharp knife into uniform bite‑size pinwheel pieces. The pinwheels are arranged on a white plate, a close‑up of the finished bites is shown, and the video ends with the eHow logo over a red splash screen.
